title: RICH VS POOR MINDSET | An Eye Opening Interview with Robert Kiyosaki
summary: Interview with a rich-dad author: paychecks make you an employee, saving and getting out of debt is obsolete, use debt and real estate to pay no tax.

assertions.quote: go to school, get a job, work hard, save money, get out of debt and invest for the long-term in the stock market
when you print savers get creamed and people who work for money get creamed. When they print debtors get rich.

verdicts.note: Unexpected inflation does favor fixed-rate borrowers, but real wages and asset returns vary; 'get rich' overstates it.

assertions.quote: I put a million dollars in real estate, I get four million from the bank.

verdicts.note: In the 2019 SCF, 87.4% of middle-class assets were the own home, liquid savings and pensions, with non-home real estate a sliver split with business equity and securities, and only 12.6% of the middle 60% owned any other real estate; investment real estate is common among the top 1% (three quarters own some) but sits beside businesses and stock, so the data show rentals as one asset of the rich, not the route ordinary households take, though a cross-section cannot say how anyone became rich.

Credit-report data show mortgage borrowers with three or more first liens were safer than single owners while prices rose but much riskier after 2006, with their serious delinquencies exploding in the bust: leveraged multi-property buying worked only while prices rose, though the investors studied include short-horizon speculators, not only cash-flow landlords.

assertions.quote: The moment you take that paycheck you're an employee
buying your house because it's an asset and investing for a long term. It's obsolete.
when I make a million bucks, I keep a million bucks

verdicts.note: Depreciation and exchanges defer real-estate tax, but zero tax is an edge case and no employee pays a 75% rate.
Depreciation and exchanges can defer real-estate tax, but paying zero tax is an edge case, not the norm for entrepreneurs.

assertions.quote: The self-employed pay the highest taxes of all and nobody tells them that.

verdicts.note: Self-employment tax adds both halves of payroll tax, but deductions offset it; it is not clearly the highest.

assertions.quote: people who are afraid of losing their jobs they generally lose their jobs

verdicts.note: Motivational framing with no measurable mechanism.

Teenage self-esteem and an internal locus of control (believing one controls one's future rather than fate or luck) predict later becoming an incorporated entrepreneur, alongside aptitude, family income and managerial aspirations; the paper does not test whether fear of job loss leads to job loss.
